newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Cycle & Carriage falls ahead of interim results.
newsitem.headline: Cycle & Carriage falls ahead of interim results.

text.p: Shares in Property and car distributor Cycle & Carriage fell to a 12-month low of Singapore $12.50 on Wednesday afternoon on expectations of weaker 1997 earnings, dealers and analysts said.
"There is some short selling ahead of its interim results which are expected to be lower than last year," a dealer with a local brokerage said.
"Investors are also afraid the recent rise in Singapore's car quotas will squeeze margins and profits," he added.
At 0735 GMT, the shares were trading around S$12.50, down 70 cents. The drop pushed the key Straits Times Industrials Index down 20.25 points or 1.05 percent down to 1,916.84.

According to Edinburgh Publishing's Estimate Directory, net profits for the retailer which holds franchises for Mercedes Benz, Proton and Mitsubishi vehicles in Singapore, are expected to be around S$219.6 million for the year ending December 31.
Research house G.K. Goh estimated net profits at S$216 million while UBS Singapore put earnings around S$211 million.
"Earnings will be disappointing. But that's not new because the management has been warning about this. It should not come as a surprise," Lim Jit Soon, head of research at UBS, told Reuters.
In March, Cycle & Carriage said 1997 outlook was challenging due to continued competition in the passenger car market, which was expected to decline by about five percent against 1996.
Analysts maintained their "buy" or "hold" recommedations for the company.

"We believe the group could be very well positioned to ride the upturn in the motor cycle here. So while we expect the interim earnings to be fairly poor, it will probably be the worst. We expect it will grow from there on," Lim said.
"At S$12.50, the price earning ratio is 13-14 times the 1997 earnings. That is not too demanding," said investment analyst Lee Sze Mian at GK Goh. However, she added there was no hurry to buy.
Analysts said the property division would continue to be the earnings driver for the group, which should see contributions from its Merawood condominium project.
However, motor sales are expected to decline. Lim of UBS estimated a possible 15 percent drop in earnings from its motor franchise to about S$190 million this year.
Lee said Mercedes sales could fall to about 3,500 units against some 3,900 in 1996.
